questions.q: What message from God did Azariah deliver to King Asa?
questions.a: The message was that Yahweh was with Asa, while Asa was with Yahweh, but if Asa left Yahweh, Yahweh would leave Asa.

questions.q: What was Israel without for a long time?
questions.a: Israel was without the true God, a teaching priest, and the law for a long time.

questions.q: In those times, what were on all the inhabitants of the lands?
questions.a: In those times, great troubles were on all the inhabitants of the lands.

questions.q: How did God trouble the inhabitants of the lands?
questions.a: God troubled the inhabitants of the lands with all kinds of suffering.

questions.q: What did Asa rebuild when he heard the prophet’s message?
questions.a: Asa rebuilt the altar of Yahweh when he heard the prophet’s message.

questions.q: Why did great numbers of people come to King Asa from Ephraim, Manasseh, and Simeon?
questions.a: They came because they saw that Yahweh was with King Asa.

questions.q: What did the people make a covenant to do?
questions.a: The people made a covenant to seek Yahweh with all their heart and with all their soul.

questions.q: What would happen to anyone who refused to seek Yahweh?
questions.a: Anyone who refused to seek Yahweh would be put to death.

questions.q: What did Yahweh give the people after they swore to him with all their heart?
questions.a: Yahweh gave the people peace all around them.

questions.q: What was the condition of King Asa’s heart?
questions.a: King Asa’s heart was completely devoted to Yahweh all his days.

questions.q: What did not occur until Asa’s thirty-fifth year of reigning?
questions.a: There was no war until Asa’s thirty-fifth year of reigning.

commentary.text: The people make a solemn covenant with God.

—The work of complete reformation appeared so difficult, that Asa had not courage to attempt it, till assured of Divine assistance and acceptance. He and his people offered sacrifices to God; thanksgiving for the favours they had received, and supplication for further favours. Prayers and praises are now our spiritual sacrifices. The people, of their own will, covenanted to seek the Lord, each for himself, with earnestness. What is religion but seeking God, inquiring after him, applying to him upon all occasions? We make nothing of our religion, if we do not make heart-work of it; God will have all the heart, or none. Our devotedness to God our Saviour, should be avowed and shown in the most solemn and public manner. What is done in hypocrisy is a mere drudgery.
